bull_case: Commerce, fintech, credit, ads and logistics keep compounding while investment intensity normalizes, allowing owner FCF/share to scale sharply without relying on multiple expansion.
bear_case: Credit losses, free-shipping/logistics investment, funding costs and FX pressure keep margins and adjusted FCF weak even while GMV and TPV continue growing.
thesis: At $1,820.47, MELI trades below the locked Base DCF of about $1,979 but without a large conventional margin of safety. Q2 revenue grew 50%, GMV 44% and TPV 56%, yet H1 adjusted FCF fell to $158M. The valuation therefore depends on converting ecosystem growth into durable owner FCF/share as credit and logistics investment mature.

evidence.claim: MELI closed at $1,820.47 on 2026-09-21; with 50.697M shares the frozen equity value is about $92.3B.
evidence.source: StockAnalysis historical price plus Q2 2026 10-Q share count

evidence.claim: Q2 2026 net revenues and financial income were $10.169B, up 49.8% YoY; GMV rose 44% and TPV 56%.
H1 2026 operating cash flow was $5.737B but company-defined adjusted FCF was only $158M after customer-fund, lending, fintech-funding and capex adjustments.
Q2 2026 operating income was $683M, down 17.3% YoY, with a 6.7% operating margin despite nearly 50% revenue growth.
The locked 9% DCF with -$126.73 net cash/share implies about $138 Bear, $1,979 Base and $4,720 Bull; price/Base is 0.9197x.

counterevidence: FY2025 adjusted FCF was $1.481B, so H1 2026 cash compression may reflect a deliberate investment wave rather than permanent deterioration.
GMV and TPV are growing much faster than mature-market commerce/payment benchmarks, leaving significant operating leverage if investment intensity normalizes.
Credit and fintech funding complicate raw CFO interpretation; neither GAAP CFO nor simple capex subtraction is a clean owner-FCF proxy.
A large share of revenue is generated in Brazil, Mexico and Argentina, making USD valuation sensitive to FX and sovereign conditions.
unknowns: Normalized adjusted FCF margin after the current logistics and credit investment wave.
Steady-state credit loss ratio and risk-adjusted return on the loan book.
Long-run shipping subsidy/free-delivery economics in Brazil and Mexico.
Consistent five-year valuation percentile on a reproducible metric.
falsifiers: Adjusted FCF/share fails to recover despite continued GMV and TPV growth.
Credit losses and funding costs rise faster than financial income for several quarters.
A realistic Bull owner-FCF/share path no longer values shares above market.
